newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican rebels on recruitment drive, painter freed.
newsitem.headline: Mexican rebels on recruitment drive, painter freed.

text.p: Scores of armed rebel troops surrounded a town in the southern state of Oaxaca, bursting into the town hall and holding a propaganda rally in a bid to recruit fighters, local authorities said on Sunday.
The action on Saturday night in this town some 40 miles (60 kms) southwest of Oaxaca City coincided with the freeing of a left-wing painter who had been abducted at gunpoint four days earlier.

Human rights workers in Oaxaca say suspected police intelligence groups have seized at gunpoint and held incommunicado 12 left-wing activists, accusing them of belonging to the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR). All later were freed.
Recently, the rebels have limited their operations to propaganda blitzes and mostly have avoided conflict.

Journalists, tipped off that there was to be an EPR action in San Miguel Peras, saw rebel slogans painted on homes and basketball courts in the mountain-top Indian town, but the rebels had left before the reporters arrived.
Local officials said they alerted authorities immediately after the rebels had departed, but police and troops failed to turn up until more than three hours later.

They said masked EPR fighters, armed with AK-47 assault rifles, held a meeting in the town square to recruit potential supporters. Locals, who said they were not frightened, came out of their houses to listen.
Around 100 other guerrillas surrounded the town, and a delegation of four EPR leaders entered the town hall to discuss their struggle with local councilmen.

"They told them not to be afraid," one local official who asked not to be identified said. But he also said the EPR rebels appeared jumpy. "They had voices like adolescents. They were insecure, they spoke very quietly."

The action in San Migel Peras was on the last day of what the rebels had previously announced would be a limited propaganda campaign ending Feb 15. It was not clear what the next phase of the rebel strategy would be.

In Oaxaca City on Sunday, relatives of the abducted painter, 47-year-old Niceforo Urbieta, said he was resting and nursing a recurring kidney problem after his 96-hour kidnap, and that he had not yet explained what had happened to him.
He turned up on foot at his mother's house on Saturday night, looking "physically and mentally exhausted," his sister Herminia Urbieta Morales said.
